videos.script:
Last lesson changed the page. Today the page talks back. {{event}} Every click, every key, every letter typed into a field is an event, and a script can ask to hear about any of them.

You ask with addEventListener. {{listener}} Name the event, hand over a function, and the browser calls it each time. That part takes five minutes.

{{journey}} The part that takes longer is where an event goes. A click on a button is not only a click on the button. It is also a click on the list the button is in, and on the page around that, and the browser visits each of them, down and then back up. {{delegate}} That journey is why one listener on a list can handle every button in it, including buttons added later.

{{forms}} Then forms: stopping the browser's own reaction to a submit, reading every field at once, and letting the browser check the fields before your code does. {{keyboard}} And the keyboard, because a page that only works with a mouse is a page some of your users cannot use.
